figures.title: Current sense against clamp reference
figures.blurb: The ESC's own current reading, compared with a clamp meter on the battery lead at six throttle holds.

series.name: Clamp meter on the battery lead

figures.setup: One OpenESC-20x20 on the bench with one motor driven from the bench controller. A DC clamp meter on the battery lead is the reference. Six throttle holds of 8 to 20 s each, from 150 to 1000 permille.

source.reduction: One median per throttle hold over the settled window; frames in throttle or speed transients are excluded.

figures.finding: Before the rev3.2 input network, the ESC read 2.6 times the clamp at 150 permille (1.03 A against 0.39 A), 0.36 times at 800 permille and 1.16 times at 1000 permille (64.7 A against 55.7 A). The error changes size and direction with throttle.
caveats: One unit, one run.
The clamp is reference grade below 40 A; the 1000 permille point is above that.
No capture exists after the rev3.2 input network, so this figure shows the state before the change only.

figures.title: Die temperature in a ramp to destruction
figures.blurb: Die temperature against clamp current while one channel was ramped to full throttle with no thermal guard.
figures.setup: One OpenESC-20x20, channel 4 driven alone. Throttle ramped from 0 to full over 120 s with the thermal limit disabled, fan cooling and a fresh pack. The plot ends where the bus voltage telemetry reads zero.

source.reduction: Logged frames from 8 s to the loss of bus voltage telemetry, kept as the minimum and maximum of 170 time buckets.

figures.finding: The die reading rose from 23 C to 156 C while the clamp current climbed to 39.8 A. The die peaked at 161 C 1.4 s later, after the motor had stopped drawing load and the current had fallen to 10.6 A. Bus voltage telemetry reads zero from 104 s.
caveats: Single channel, one unit, run to destruction with no thermal guard.
The die sensor is the controller's own temperature sensor, not a measurement of the output transistors.
Why the load collapsed at 101 s is not established by this capture.
The clamp reads about -0.85 A with no current flowing; the offset is not removed.

figures.title: Current sense against clamp reference, 30x30
figures.blurb: The ESC's own current reading against a clamp meter during a throttle sweep.

series.name: Clamp meter on the battery lead

figures.setup: One OpenESC-30x30 driving four motors on a 13 inch load rig, throttle swept up and back down. A DC clamp meter on the battery lead is the reference. The plot stops at the last throttle bin with a clamp reading (86 A; the clamp's range is 100 A).

source.reduction: Sweep bins of mechanical speed; up and down legs averaged in each bin.

figures.finding: Where the clamp reads, the ESC read 1.16 to 1.46 times the clamp in each throttle bin, between 1.25 and 1.35 in 26 of 36 bins.
caveats: One sweep on one board.
That the board is an OpenESC-30x30 is the operator's statement; its revision is not in the capture.
Up and down legs of the sweep differ by up to 10 A.
Held for founder review before publication.

figures.title: Flight log, four airframes
figures.blurb: Throttle stick command in the longest retained flight of each of four airframes, all recorded by the OpenFC-Lite stack on one day.
figures.setup: Blackbox logs from four airframes flown on 2026-08-09, each with the full OpenDrone stack. The longest retained flight of each airframe is shown: 291 s, 377 s, 143 s and 513 s.

source.reduction: Logged throttle command, kept as the minimum and maximum of 150 time buckets per flight.

figures.finding: Peak throttle command was 1413 us (3 inch), 1408 us (5 inch freestyle), 2000 us (5 inch race) and 1945 us (8 inch).
caveats: This is a flight log from one pilot on one day, not a flight controller measurement. No FC bench capture exists.
The longest flight was kept for log retention, not as the most demanding flight of each airframe.
The values are the pilot's throttle command, not motor output.

figures.title: Thrust against rotor speed
figures.blurb: Thrust stand sweep from 10 to 100 percent throttle in ten holds.
figures.setup: Thrust stand with a load cell calibrated on the controller. Ten throttle holds of about 4 s from 10 to 100 percent. Motor, propeller, ESC and pack are not recorded for the main run; the second run lists its motor as OpenMotor-2306. Rotor speed is the ESC's electrical speed divided by 7 pole pairs, the pole count stored in the capture.

source.reduction: Median of the last 2 s of each throttle hold; the band is the 25th to 75th percentile over the same window. Holds with no pack voltage reading are dropped.

figures.finding: From 40 percent throttle up, thrust is about 1.7 g per krpm squared (1.67 to 1.74 across the main run). The main run reaches 1496 g at 100 percent throttle and 29350 rpm. At the same speed the second run reads 2 to 3 percent less thrust, with a pack voltage up to 1.9 V higher.
caveats: One capture per run; the main run was not repeated.
Motor, propeller, ESC and pack are not recorded for the main run.
The clamp meter was not recorded.
The load-cell scale comes from the controller's stored calibration; no independent weight check is recorded in the capture.
The second run ends at 70 percent: the pack was pulled mid-run, so its later holds are dropped.

figures.title: Rotor speed by throttle
figures.blurb: Rotor speed at each throttle hold.
figures.setup: Same two thrust stand runs as the thrust figure. Rotor speed is the ESC's electrical speed divided by 7 pole pairs.

source.reduction: Median of the last 2 s of each throttle hold. Holds with no pack voltage reading are dropped.

figures.finding: Rotor speed rises from about 5000 rpm at 10 percent to 29350 rpm at 100 percent in the main run.
caveats: One capture per run.
Motor, propeller, ESC and pack are not recorded for the main run.

figures.title: Thrust by throttle
figures.setup: Same two thrust stand runs as the thrust figure, with the load cell calibrated on the controller.

source.reduction: Median of the last 2 s of each throttle hold. Holds with no pack voltage reading are dropped.

figures.finding: Thrust is 30 g at 10 percent and 1496 g at 100 percent in the main run.
caveats: One capture per run.
At 10 percent the main run reads 30 g and the second 35 g, a difference of about 17 percent at a low load.
The clamp meter was not recorded.

figures.title: Pack voltage by throttle
figures.blurb: Pack voltage at each throttle hold.
figures.setup: Same two thrust stand runs as the thrust figure. Pack voltage is read by the ESC.

source.reduction: Median of the last 2 s of each throttle hold. Holds with no pack voltage reading are dropped.

figures.finding: The pack sags from 24.4 V at 10 percent to 19.3 V at 100 percent in the main run. The second run starts about 0.3 V higher and is 1.9 V higher at 70 percent.
caveats: The packs are not recorded; the second run reads higher throughout.
Voltage is the ESC's own reading, not checked against a meter.

figures.title: ESC temperature by throttle
figures.blurb: Hottest ESC die reading at each throttle hold.
figures.setup: Same two thrust stand runs as the thrust figure. Temperature is the hottest of the ESC's reported die readings.

source.reduction: Median of the last 2 s of each throttle hold. Holds with no pack voltage reading are dropped.

figures.finding: The hottest die reading rises from 44 C at 10 percent to 72 C at 100 percent in the main run; the second run stays between 42 and 48 C up to 70 percent.
caveats: The main run was hotter at the same throttle; motor, propeller, cooling and packs are not recorded.
The die sensor is the controller's own, not a measurement of the output transistors.

figures.title: RSSI against distance, Gemini and Mono
figures.blurb: One 75 minute ride out to 5.3 km with a Gemini and a Mono on the same carry.
figures.setup: One OpenRX-Gemini and one OpenRX-Mono on the same carry, logged together during a ride out along a road to 5.3 km. Distance is measured from the start of the GPS track, not from the transmitter.

source.reduction: Median of the logged RSSI in 100 m distance bins; the band is the 25th to 75th percentile.

figures.finding: From 2.9 km to 5.3 km the Gemini's reported RSSI is below the Mono's in all 25 of the 100 m bins that both logged: a median of 4 dB lower, up to 7 dB, and 2 dB or more lower in 23 of the 25. Below 1.3 km the two are within about 5 dB of each other in either direction.
caveats: One unit of each, one ride.
Antenna placement on the carry may explain the gap.
RSSI is the value each receiver reports after its own antenna selection.
The receiver columns in the log are numbered, not named; which column is which unit comes from the operators' notes. One column duplicates the Mono and is excluded.
Transmitter settings and receiver firmware are not recorded.
No transmitter position or terrain is recorded, so range is not line-of-sight range.

figures.title: Link quality and RSSI at the first link drop
figures.blurb: RSSI and link quality of the Lite as the ride passed out of range for the first time.
figures.setup: One OpenRX-Lite in the same ride as the distance figure, 120 s around the first link drop.

source.reduction: Logged values from 200 s to 320 s, unreduced.

figures.finding: RSSI fell from -74 dBm at 284 s to -98 dBm at 294.5 s. Link quality held at 87 percent or more until 292.6 s, then fell to 17 percent at 305.8 s, when RSSI had reached -104 dBm. An earlier dip to -91 dBm at 263 s cost link quality only 10 points and recovered.
caveats: One unit, one ride.
That this column is the Lite follows the operators' hand markers; the log does not name its receivers.
Transmitter settings and receiver firmware are not recorded.

figures.title: Gemini antenna 2 use against distance
figures.blurb: How often the Gemini selected its second antenna along the ride.

series.name: Share of logged samples on antenna 2

figures.setup: One OpenRX-Gemini, same ride as the distance figure. The log records which of its two antennas was active in each sample.

source.reduction: Share of logged samples with antenna 2 active in 500 m distance bins.

figures.finding: Antenna 2 is not selected in the first 1 km. Its share is 10 to 16 percent of samples between 1.5 and 4 km, 22 percent from 4.5 to 5 km and 35 percent from 5 km to the end of the track.
caveats: One unit, one ride.
Samples are not evenly spread over distance: bins hold 9 to 871 samples, and bins with fewer than 8 are dropped.
Antenna placement and orientation are not recorded.
